subject: Confidence intervals for CFI and RMSEA difference

messages.author: 572119bb37de95d7
messages.subject: Confidence intervals for CFI and RMSEA difference
parts:
I came across a very interesting paper on model comparisons:

Lai, K. (2019). Confidence Interval for RMSEA or CFI Difference Between Nonnested Models. Structural Equation Modeling: A Multidisciplinary Journal, 27(1), 16–32. https://doi.org/10.1080/10705511.2019.1631704

Here's the abstract:

In addition to evaluating a single model, often one also uses RMSEA and CFI to compare the
fit of multiple candidate models. Model selection based on ΔRMSEA and ΔCFI can be
meaningful because (a) showing a model is better than another is more scientific and easier
than showing a model is “good;” (b) it avoids the problems with cutoffs for fit indices; (c)
one is less likely to overlook other equally substantively plausible models. However,
currently, such model selection is based on sample ΔRMSEA and sample ΔCFI, which
can be much smaller, much larger, or even of opposite sign than the population values.
Accordingly, we propose analytic confidence intervals for population ΔRMSEA and ΔCFI.
The methods are applicable to both nonnested and nested models, robust to nonnormal data,
computationally efficient, and do not assume any candidate model is true. Simulation studies
verified our proposed methods are trustworthy

To me, this approach seems very promising. Is the suggestion by Lai something that could be implemented in semTools? Please see the paper for further details. The important parts are sections with technical details, but the paper also has awell-written introduction on problems in relying on cuttoffs for fit indices.

Christopher Bratt

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: Confidence intervals for CFI and RMSEA difference
parts: Is the suggestion by Lai something that could be implemented in semTools?

If you would like to write the syntax and make a contribution, I would be happy to review it for inclusion in semTools.  But from my reading of the paper, it did not resolve the issue of arbitrarily defining "important misspecification" in RMSEA-units or CFI-units.  That is a much bigger problem for using fixed cutoffs than mere sampling error.

Terrence D. Jorgensen
Assistant Professor, Methods and Statistics
Research Institute for Child Development and Education, the University of Amsterdam
http://www.uva.nl/profile/t.d.jorgensen

messages.subject: Re: Confidence intervals for CFI and RMSEA difference
parts: I don't think it intended to solve the issue of arbitrary cutoffs, but to sidestep it by comparing non-nested models rather than relying on a test of a single model.
